story.title: Avalanche in Pakistan Claims Lives of 10 Climbers, Including Nirmal Purja
story.summary: A powerful avalanche struck Broad Peak in Pakistan, resulting in the deaths of 10 climbers, including renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja. The climbers lost contact with their base camp during their ascent. Purja, known for his record-breaking climbs, was leading the expedition when the avalanche occurred.

event_overview.title: About Mountaineering Incident
event_overview.subject: Mountaineering Incident
event_overview.summary: This event concerns an avalanche that struck a 10-person climbing expedition on Broad Peak in Pakistan’s Karakoram range on July 30, 2026. The expedition included high-altitude climber Nirmal Purja; by August 1, the expedition company said all 10 climbers had died while recovery efforts continued.

facts.label: Incident date and reported toll
facts.value: The avalanche occurred on July 30, 2026. On August 1, Elite Exped, the expedition company, said that Purja and the other nine climbers in the group had died.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Broad Peak is an approximately 8,051-meter mountain in the Karakoram, on the Pakistan-China border and near K2; it is among the world’s fourteen mountains above 8,000 meters.

facts.label: Expedition
facts.value: The affected party was a 10-member expedition led by Nepal-born mountaineer Nirmal Purja, also known as Nims Dai; Pakistani rescuers began searching in severe conditions after the avalanche.

facts.label: Mountaineering oversight
facts.value: Climbing and trekking activity in Gilgit-Baltistan is regulated by the regional tourism authorities: expeditions require registration and permits in restricted areas, and the government states that the Department of Tourism is the authority issuing climbing permits.

facts.label: Permit category
facts.value: Pakistan’s Gilgit-Baltistan tourism rules place peaks from 8,001 to 8,500 meters in a permit-and-royalty category; Broad Peak falls within that elevation band.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows the immediate avalanche, searches, recoveries and reported deaths; it does not aim to cover the full Broad Peak climbing season, all expeditions on the mountain, or any later technical investigation into the avalanche.

explore_lenses.label: What is known about how the avalanche hit?
explore_lenses.title: A high-altitude collapse cut off the team
explore_lenses.summary: The best available accounts place the avalanche between camps 2 and 3 on Broad Peak's west-ridge route, after the climbers had begun their summit push. The precise trigger and whether more than one avalanche occurred were not established as of August 1.

claims.text: The Alpine Club of Pakistan said the team lost contact with base camp after the avalanche on Thursday, July 30, while attempting Broad Peak.
Tracker data reviewed by reporters indicated a rapid loss of altitude near 6,579 meters between camps 2 and 3; this supports, but does not independently establish, the reported avalanche location.
Naila Kiani of the Alpine Club of Pakistan said it was possible two avalanches struck, but that only one had been confirmed at that point.

explore_lenses.label: Why does Purja's death matter to climbing?
explore_lenses.title: It removes a prominent 8,000-meter leader
explore_lenses.summary: Purja was not only a well-known climber but the expedition leader and co-founder of its operator. The deaths also underscore that Broad Peak, despite being marketed as comparatively accessible among 8,000-meter mountains, remains an extreme high-altitude objective.

claims.text: Purja led the expedition and had climbed all 14 peaks above 8,000 meters in 189 days in 2019; he also helped lead the first winter ascent of K2 in 2021.
Elite Exped, the company Purja co-founded, described Broad Peak as a strenuous 8,047-meter climb intended for experienced climbers with prior 6,000- or 7,000-meter ascents.
The expedition included climbers and guides from Nepal, Oman, the United States, Pakistan and China, illustrating that the consequences extend across several national climbing communities.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in the recovery effort?
explore_lenses.title: Recovery continues, constrained by weather
explore_lenses.summary: By August 1, all 10 members of the expedition had been confirmed dead, but recovery operations were still underway. The immediate priorities were retrieving remains, identifying all victims and returning bodies to families, subject to weather and access on the mountain.

claims.text: Elite Exped said all 10 climbers swept away had died; Karrar Haidri, vice president of the Alpine Club of Pakistan, confirmed the deaths to AP.
Rescuers had found four bodies and recovered three by July 31; military helicopters were involved, but harsh weather hindered flights.
As of August 1, search teams were attempting to recover the remaining bodies; no public timetable for completing the operation was reported.

story_report.summary: An avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak killed 10 climbers, including expedition leader Nirmal Purja, after the team lost contact with base camp while attempting the mountain on July 30. The deaths were confirmed by the Alpine Club of Pakistan and Elite Exped, the company Purja co-founded. Rescue teams located four bodies and recovered three by July 31, while harsh weather restricted helicopter operations and complicated efforts to retrieve those still on the mountain.

sections.heading: Purja’s Broad Peak Expedition
sections.body: Purja led the expedition on Broad Peak, an 8,047-meter mountain that Elite Exped describes as a strenuous objective for experienced climbers with prior high-altitude ascents. He was known for climbing all 14 mountains above 8,000 meters in 189 days in 2019 and for helping lead the first winter ascent of K2 in 2021. The expedition included climbers and guides from Nepal, Oman, the United States, Pakistan and China.

sections.heading: Recovery Effort Faces Mountain Conditions
sections.body: As of August 1, search teams were attempting to recover the remaining bodies, with no public timetable reported for completing the operation. Military helicopters were involved in the response, but harsh weather hindered flights. The duration of the effort could depend on weather, terrain, and the number and identities of remains still awaiting recovery.

unresolved.text: Authorities and the expedition company had not publicly identified what triggered the avalanche or confirmed whether a second slide occurred. An Alpine Club of Pakistan official said two avalanches were possible, but only one had been confirmed at that point.

related_stories.title: Explosion at Moscow restaurant results in three fatalities and multiple injuries
related_stories.summary: An explosion occurred at a restaurant in central Moscow, killing three people and injuring at least 15 others. Security officials reported that a woman attempted to enter the restaurant with explosives but was stopped by a security guard before the device detonated. Investigators and emergency services are currently at the scene.

related_stories.title: Vincent Pastore, known for his role in 'The Sopranos,' passes away at 80
related_stories.summary: Vincent Pastore, who portrayed Salvatore 'Big Pussy' Bonpensiero on HBO's 'The Sopranos,' has died at the age of 80. His passing was confirmed by his manager, who stated that he died at his home in The Bronx. Pastore was a prominent figure in the series, which aired from 1999 to 2007.
